findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: jp-invoice-check, tenders, uk-tenders, fr-tenders, au-contracts, wallet-risk, read, crawl, jobs, domain-profile · Private data: jp-invoice-check, sanctions-screen, tenders, uk-tenders, fr-tenders, au-contracts, wallet-risk, read, crawl, domain-profile · Public sink: jp-invoice-check, au-contracts, wallet-risk · Destructive: jp-invoice-check.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: jp-invoice-check, tenders, uk-tenders, fr-tenders, au-contracts, wallet-risk, read, crawl, jobs, domain-profile · Private data: jp-invoice-check, sanctions-screen, tenders, uk-tenders, fr-tenders, au-contracts, wallet-risk, read, crawl, domain-profile · Public sink: jp-invoice-check, au-contracts, wallet-risk · Destructive: jp-invoice-check

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
